description: Fictional decided past risks seeded into the evaluation database before any golden case runs. Each key is referenced by expected_similar_past in risk_golden_set.json.

decisions.title: Admin console reachable without multi-factor authentication
decisions.description: The internal administration console for customer accounts accepts a username and password only. A phished or reused password gives full control over customer records and refunds.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for every admin console login and block password-only sessions.
decisions.rationale: Password-only admin access is not acceptable for a system that can issue refunds. Multi-factor authentication rollout approved with a 14-day deadline and hardware keys for super-admins.

decisions.title: Nightly database backups never restored in a test
decisions.description: Backups of the orders database run every night but nobody has restored one in two years. Corrupted or incomplete backups would only be discovered during a real outage.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Run a monthly automated restore into an isolated environment and alert when restored row counts differ from production.
decisions.rationale: Untested backups give false assurance. Monthly automated restore tests approved, and the first test must complete before the next quarterly board report.

decisions.title: Payroll provider without a current SOC 2 report
decisions.description: The external payroll provider processes salary and bank details for all employees, but its SOC 2 Type II report expired eight months ago and a new audit has not been scheduled.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Amend the contract to add breach liability and indemnity clauses, require a new SOC 2 report within six months, and add the provider to the cyber insurance schedule.
decisions.rationale: Replacing the provider mid-year is impractical. Financial exposure is transferred through contract liability terms and the cyber insurance policy, with a six-month deadline for the new SOC 2 report.

decisions.title: Staff repeatedly fail phishing simulations
decisions.description: Quarterly phishing simulations show that one in four employees clicks the link and one in ten enters credentials. Credential theft through email is the most likely way in for attackers.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Introduce short mandatory training after each failed simulation, add a report-phishing button to the mail client, and enforce multi-factor authentication for webmail.
decisions.rationale: Human error is the main entry point. Targeted training plus multi-factor authentication on webmail approved, and the click rate is reported to the risk committee each quarter.

decisions.title: Field sales laptops without disk encryption
decisions.description: Laptops issued to the field sales team were set up without full disk encryption. They store customer contact exports and are often used in hotels and trains, where loss or theft is common.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Enable full disk encryption through device management, block unencrypted devices from the VPN, and enable remote wipe.
decisions.rationale: A lost laptop with customer exports is a reportable breach. Encryption enforced through device management is low cost and approved for completion within 30 days.

decisions.title: Campaign microsites on an end-of-life CMS
decisions.description: Old campaign microsites still run on a content management system that stopped receiving security patches last year. Several known remote code execution flaws affect the installed version.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Decommission the legacy microsites, redirect their domains to the main website, and archive the content offline.
decisions.rationale: The sites get no meaningful traffic and cannot be patched. Decommissioning removes the exposure entirely, and no budget is approved for further maintenance.

decisions.title: On-premise server room below the flood line
decisions.description: The remaining on-premise server room is in the basement of the head office, which sits in a flood zone. Most production workloads have moved to the cloud, but the file server and phone system remain.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Confirm that property insurance covers equipment and business interruption, and keep the migration of the remaining systems on the cloud roadmap.
decisions.rationale: Relocation costs exceed the remaining exposure. Equipment and business interruption losses are covered by the property insurance policy, and the residual risk is reviewed every year.

decisions.title: Marketing wiki pages shared through public links
decisions.description: The marketing team shares wiki pages with agencies through public links that do not require sign-in. The pages contain published brand guidelines and campaign calendars.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Accept the practice for non-confidential content, set links to expire after 30 days, and review shared pages each quarter.
decisions.rationale: The content is already public or of low sensitivity. Accepted with link expiry and a quarterly review, and any page with confidential data must move to sign-in sharing.

decisions.title: Card numbers written to application debug logs
decisions.description: A debug setting left on in the checkout service writes full card numbers into application logs, which are kept for 90 days and can be read by the whole engineering team.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Disable debug logging in production, mask card numbers in the logging middleware, purge existing logs, and add a data loss prevention scan to CI.
decisions.rationale: Full card numbers in logs break PCI DSS requirements. Masking and a log purge are approved as an emergency change, and a data loss prevention check in CI prevents it from happening again.

decisions.title: Currency exposure on supplier payments in US dollars
decisions.description: Hardware suppliers invoice in US dollars while revenue is in euros. A sharp currency move between order and payment can add several percent to the cost of large purchases.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Use forward contracts with the bank for supplier payments above a set threshold.
decisions.rationale: Currency risk on payments above the threshold is transferred to the bank through forward contracts. Smaller payments are accepted at spot rates.

decisions.title: Customer login endpoint without brute force protection
decisions.description: The customer login API allows unlimited password attempts. Credential stuffing traffic using leaked password lists has been seen in the web application firewall logs.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Add per-account and per-IP rate limits, require a CAPTCHA after repeated failures, and notify users about suspicious login attempts.
decisions.rationale: Active credential stuffing makes this urgent. Rate limiting and CAPTCHA are approved, and breached password screening follows next quarter.

decisions.title: Contractor accounts left active after contracts end
decisions.description: Contractor directory accounts are disabled by hand by line managers. An access review found accounts still active months after contracts ended, some with production access.
decisions.proposed_mitigation: Set an expiry date on every contractor account when it is created and disable accounts automatically when the contract end date passes.
decisions.rationale: Manual offboarding has failed repeatedly. Automatic account expiry tied to the contract end date is approved.
